name: SNK retroactive referral reward accounting
summary: SNKMiner.dynamicEarned() pays a parent its children's current staked balance times the whole reward-per-token growth since the parent's last update. After pre-staking small parent accounts, the attacker flash-borrowed SNK, staked it through freshly bound child contracts, claimed each parent's inflated referral reward, exited and repaid, repeating over four transactions.
notes: The exploit binds new child contracts through SNKMiner.bindParent(), which calls Invite.invite() and only works because the deployer made SNKMiner an Invite minter after deployment; that role grant is the reset. The later setPool (ref) only halved the reward rate, which changes the loss size.

The attacker's parent accounts were staked days earlier (setup, no loss); the four exploit transactions each drained SNKMiner, the last also sold all SNK. SNK is unpriced: valued at the USDT realised, pro rata net of the 1,950 SNK the attacker staked in setup and withdrew.
